app.name: Google Maps
app.description: Real-time GPS navigation, traffic, transit, and local exploration with Street View and reviews.

verdict.one_liner: Google Maps tracks your precise location when you use it and uses it for targeted ads.
verdict.summary: Google Maps collects your precise GPS location, sensor data, Wi-Fi access points, cell towers, and Bluetooth devices when you use the service. This data is used for driving directions, search results, and personalized ads based on your location. Your data is shared across Google services and may be retained even after deletion. Some data is shared with affiliates, partners, and for legal reasons.
verdict.recommendation_reason: Google Maps collects extensive location data when you use it for directions and shows personalized ads based on your location. Use device location controls and consider limiting Google Account activity sharing.

red.title: Precise location tracked during use
red.plain_english: Google Maps collects your GPS, sensor data, IP address, Wi-Fi access points, cell towers, and Bluetooth devices when you use the service to provide directions and ads based on your location.

red.title: Location used for targeted ads
red.plain_english: Google uses your location data to show you personalized ads based on where you are and your activity across Google services.

red.title: Data used across Google services
red.plain_english: Google may use the information it collects from Maps across other Google services and devices.

red.title: Some data kept after deletion
red.plain_english: You can delete some location data, but Google may retain it for longer periods for legal or security reasons.

green.title: You can export and delete data
green.plain_english: You can export or delete your content from specific Google services, including Maps.

green.title: Location settings can be managed
green.plain_english: You can turn off location access in your device settings.

categories.label: Camera & Microphone
categories.plain_english: Google may save audio recordings when you interact with Maps. The policy does not clearly explain camera use.
categories.detail: The general Google Privacy Policy explicitly states audio recordings may be saved when you interact with Google Search, Assistant, and Maps. It is silent on whether Maps uses your camera.
categories.policy_excerpt: For example, you can choose whether you want Google to save an audio recording to your Google Account when you interact with Google Search, Assistant, and Maps.
concerns: Audio recording explicitly mentioned for Maps

categories.label: Location & GPS
categories.plain_english: Google Maps collects your precise location using GPS, sensors, Wi-Fi, and Bluetooth when you use the app to get directions and nearby search results.
categories.detail: The general Google Privacy Policy describes location collection including GPS, sensor data, IP address, Wi-Fi access points, cell towers, and Bluetooth devices when you use its services. This is used for driving directions, nearby search results, and ads based on location.
categories.policy_excerpt: We collect location information when you use our services, which helps us offer features like driving directions, search results for things near you, and ads based on your location. Depending on the products you're using and settings you choose, Google may use different types of location information to help make some services and products you use more helpful. These include: GPS and other sensor data from your device; IP address; Activity on Google services, such as from your searches or places you label like home or work; Information about things near your device, such as Wi-Fi access points, cell towers, and Bluetooth-enabled devices.

categories.label: Contacts & Phonebook
categories.plain_english: The policy does not mention whether Google Maps accesses your phone contacts.
categories.detail: The general Google Privacy Policy mentions suggesting recipients from contacts when sharing content, but does not explicitly state whether Maps accesses contacts.
concerns: Policy silent on contact access for Maps

categories.label: Storage & File Access
categories.plain_english: The policy does not mention whether Google Maps accesses files or photos stored on your device.
categories.detail: The general Google Privacy Policy discusses content you create, upload, or receive, but does not specify whether Maps accesses local device files or photos.
concerns: Policy silent on Maps file access

categories.label: Data Sharing with 3rd Parties
categories.plain_english: Google may share your information with affiliates, partners, and for legal reasons.
categories.detail: The general policy lists consent, domain administrators, external processing with affiliates/service providers, and legal reasons as cases for sharing personal information. Non-personally identifiable information may be shared with partners.
categories.policy_excerpt: We do not share your personal information with companies, organizations, or individuals outside of Google except in the following cases: With your consent; With domain administrators; For external processing; For legal reasons.
concerns: Data shared with affiliates and partners

categories.label: Account & Identity Data
categories.plain_english: You can use some Maps features without signing in, but a Google Account is required for saved places and location history.
categories.detail: The general policy states many Google services can be used without an account. For Maps, core navigation may work without signing in, but features like saved places and location history require a Google Account.
categories.policy_excerpt: You can use many Google services when you're signed out or without creating an account at all.
concerns: Location linked to identity when signed in

categories.label: Behavioural & Ad Tracking
categories.plain_english: Google uses your location and activity across services to show you personalized ads.
categories.detail: The general policy explicitly states location is used for ads and that personalized ads may be shown based on interests and activity across Google services.
categories.policy_excerpt: ads based on your location. Depending on your settings, we may also show you personalized ads based on your interests and activity across Google services.

categories.label: Children's Data Handling
categories.plain_english: Google offers Family Link for children under 13.
categories.detail: The general policy references Family Link for children under the applicable age.
categories.policy_excerpt: Google Accounts Managed with Family Link, for Children under 13 (or applicable age in your country)

categories.label: Network & Internet Activity
categories.plain_english: Google collects your IP address, crash reports, and activity data when you use Maps, and may use your IP to estimate your location for ads.
categories.detail: The general policy lists IP address, crash reports, system activity, and referrer URL as collected interaction data. IP address may be used for location estimation and ads.
categories.policy_excerpt: We also collect information about the interaction of your apps, browsers, and devices with our services, including IP address, crash reports, system activity, and the date, time, and referrer URL of your request.
concerns: IP used for location inference and ads

categories.label: Device Info & Fingerprinting
categories.plain_english: Google collects sensor data like accelerometer and gyroscope from your device to understand your movement, along with unique identifiers.
categories.detail: The general policy explicitly mentions sensors including accelerometer and gyroscope to determine speed and direction of travel. It also collects unique identifiers, device type, OS, carrier, and application version.
categories.policy_excerpt: Your device may have sensors that can be used to better understand your location and movement. For example, an accelerometer can be used to determine your speed and a gyroscope to figure out your direction of travel. The information we collect includes unique identifiers, browser type and settings, device type and settings, operating system, mobile network information including carrier name and phone number, and application version number.
concerns: Sensor data used for movement tracking

categories.label: Health & Biometric Data
categories.plain_english: The policy does not mention whether Google Maps collects health or biometric data.
categories.detail: Neither the general Google Privacy Policy nor the provided text mentions health or biometric data collection in the context of Maps.
concerns: Policy silent on health/biometric data for Maps

categories.label: Financial & Payment Data
categories.plain_english: The policy does not mention whether Google Maps collects payment or financial information.
categories.detail: The general Google Privacy Policy mentions shipping address and delivery instructions when purchasing services or physical goods, but does not specifically state whether Maps collects payment information.
concerns: Policy silent on Maps payment collection

categories.label: Data Deletion & User Rights
categories.plain_english: You can delete some Maps data, but Google may retain it for legal or security reasons.
categories.detail: The general policy states some data can be deleted, while other data is retained for longer periods for legitimate business or legal purposes.
categories.policy_excerpt: Some data you can delete whenever you like... And some data we retain for longer periods of time when necessary for legitimate business or legal purposes.

categories.label: Policy Change Notification
categories.plain_english: Google promises not to reduce your rights under its Privacy Policy without your explicit consent, and it publishes the date of changes with archived versions available.
categories.detail: The general Google Privacy Policy states it will not reduce your rights without explicit consent, indicates the date of last changes, offers access to archived versions, and provides more prominent notice for significant changes.
categories.policy_excerpt: We change this Privacy Policy from time to time. We will not reduce your rights under this Privacy Policy without your explicit consent. We always indicate the date the last changes were published and we offer access to archived versions for your review. If changes are significant, we'll provide a more prominent notice.
